identity.name: Shelf-Staged Privilege-Escalation Enumeration Under a Service Identity (T1082)
identity.summary: A web-server service account (www-data, causality owner apache2) spawns a shell and runs privilege-escalation enumeration tooling staged and checksummed by the DC's own SimCore rather than curled from GitHub on the customer's endpoint. Cortex XDR should detect the BEHAVIOUR — interpreter spawn, discovery breadth burst, /etc and /proc read fan-out, SUID sweep — not the tool's filename.
identity.description:
This card exists to separate two claims a POV constantly conflates: 'Cortex recognised a tool called linpeas' and 'Cortex detected privilege-escalation enumeration'. Only the second is coverage.

Delivery. Every tier-4 adapter in this engine installs its tool from the public internet ON THE TARGET at dispatch. Customers who buy Cortex run default-deny egress, so that is the first thing their network blocks — and a step whose tool never arrived RUNS ANYWAY, produces no detection, and the absent detection reads in the POV report as 'Cortex missed it'. SIM-EDR-022 is delivered the other way round: the console stages the tool onto the DC's SimCore from a commit/tag-pinned URL, composes a digest-bound plan, and the enrolled beacon fetches and sha256-verifies it against the digest it carried IN before executing. Step-01 is a hard preflight that exits non-zero with PAYLOAD_NOT_STAGED_ON_TARGET rather than degrading gracefully, because a graceful degradation here is precisely the manufactured false negative.

Detection. Nine BIOCs ship. Seven are behavioural and key on identity, causality lineage, path root, read fan-out and command breadth — none of them names a tool. Two (plus two filename IOCs) are deliberately filename-keyed and are labelled NEGATIVE-CONTROL TARGET: they fire on the canonical run and are expected to go dark once the artifact is staged under an operator-chosen basename. Three sha256 IOCs are included precisely because a rename changes the destination and never the bytes, so a hash indicator is the one atomic detection that survives the control. If a renamed run darkens the behavioural rules too, the finding is that the customer's endpoint coverage is name-keyed.

techniques.name: Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism: Setuid and Setgid
Command and Scripting Interpreter: Unix Shell

execution.framework_reference_id: T1082 — automated Linux privilege-escalation enumeration (LinPEAS / pspy / SUID3NUM) executed by a web-server service account from a staging directory.

prerequisites.description: Cortex XDR Linux agent installed and reporting on the target endpoint.
prerequisites.check_command: systemctl is-active cortex-agent || ps aux | grep -i cortex

prerequisites.description: The payload shelf carries linpeas.sh, pspy64 and suid3num.py, pinned to the digests in tools/packs/{linpeas,pspy,suid3num}.yml. Verify BEFORE the customer is watching.
An enrolled beacon whose capabilities include artifact fetch (pull mode), or a generated bash bundle on a target that DOES have public-internet egress (push mode).

A POSIX target with `python3` on PATH and a LOGIN-CAPABLE www-data account. Both were found missing on a bare ubuntu:22.04 during the 2026-08-05 beacon proof: no python3 made step-04 exit 127, and www-data's /usr/sbin/nologin shell made `runuser -l www-data` refuse before any step ran. Both fail LOUDLY, which is correct — but a DC should discover them here, not in front of a customer.
prerequisites.check_command: command -v python3 && getent passwd www-data | grep -qv nologin

payload.code:
# step-1: Shelf preflight — refuse to proceed without the staged tooling (fail loudly)
# This step exists to convert a silent no-op into a loud failure. If the
# artifacts are absent, every later step would still "run", produce no
# detection, and the run would read as a Cortex miss.
MISSING=""
for f in /tmp/linpeas.sh /tmp/pspy64 /tmp/suid3num.py; do
  [ -s "$f" ] || MISSING="$MISSING $f"
done
if [ -n "$MISSING" ]; then
  echo "[SIM-EDR-022][FATAL] PAYLOAD_NOT_STAGED_ON_TARGET:$MISSING" >&2
  echo "[SIM-EDR-022] The TTP did NOT run. Do not read the absent detections as a Cortex miss." >&2
  echo "[SIM-EDR-022] pull mode: SimCore must compose and the beacon must fetch+verify from /api/shelf/payload/<name>." >&2
  echo "[SIM-EDR-022] push mode: the bundle's adapter install section should have fetched these." >&2
  exit 1
fi
# The tool is present and verified. Record WHAT was staged, by digest, so
# the run output can be reconciled against the composition the console
# produced. sha256sum is in coreutils on every supported target.
sha256sum /tmp/linpeas.sh /tmp/pspy64 /tmp/suid3num.py
id; echo "[SIM-EDR-022] staged tooling verified under $(id -un)"
# step-2: Run the shelf-staged privilege-escalation enumerator (T1082/T1083)
/tmp/linpeas.sh -q
# step-3: Snoop the process table and cron for credentials in command lines (T1057)
timeout 20 /tmp/pspy64 -pf -i 1000
rc=$?
# 124 is `timeout` reporting it killed pspy — the designed outcome. 126/127 are
# what a missing or non-executable staged artifact produces and must still fail.
if [ "$rc" -ne 0 ] && [ "$rc" -ne 124 ]; then exit "$rc"; fi

expected_artifacts.description: A shell interpreter spawned by the web server under the www-data effective username.
expected_artifacts.expected_value: causality_actor_process_image_name = "apache2" and actor_effective_username = "www-data" and action_process_image_name in ("bash", "sh")

expected_artifacts.description: An executable under a staging root run by a non-interactive service identity.
Read fan-out across privilege-escalation-relevant paths from one causality chain.
High-rate /proc/<pid>/cmdline sweep across many distinct pids from a non-root process.
expected_artifacts.expected_value: count_distinct(action_file_path) by causality_id >= 20 where action_file_path contains "/proc/" and contains "/cmdline"

expected_artifacts.description: Filesystem-wide SUID/SGID sweep from a non-root identity.

cleanup.code:
rm -f /tmp/linpeas.sh /tmp/linpeas_output.txt /tmp/pspy64 /tmp/suid3num.py
echo '[CortexSim] SIM-EDR-022 cleanup complete — read-only enumeration only, nothing was exploited'

iocs.context: NEGATIVE-CONTROL TARGET, NOT COVERAGE. The canonical shelf filename for TOOL-LINPEAS. A renamed run stages the same verified bytes under an operator-chosen basename and this IOC correctly goes dark; the behavioural BIOCs on this card must not.
NEGATIVE-CONTROL TARGET, NOT COVERAGE. Canonical shelf filename for TOOL-PSPY.

The linpeas.sh bytes this scenario is authored against (PEASS-ng release-tag 20260803-00785084), pinned in tools/packs/linpeas.yml install.artifact.sha256. Unlike the filename IOCs above, a rename does NOT change this value — staging renames the destination, never the bytes — so a hash IOC is the one atomic indicator that survives the control.
The pspy64 bytes this scenario is authored against (pspy release-tag v1.2.1), pinned in tools/packs/pspy.yml.
The suid3num.py bytes this scenario is authored against (SUID3NUM commit 881b48866741ee78a0d79d4c54c64c53feb3f655), pinned in tools/packs/suid3num.yml.

biocs.name: EDR-022 Service Account Spawns Interpreter Under Web Server CGO
biocs.description: A non-interactive service identity (www-data/apache/nginx/nobody) spawns a shell or scripting interpreter whose causality group owner is the web server itself. BEHAVIOURAL: the web tier has no operational reason to spawn an interpreter, so this fires whatever the interpreter goes on to run — it is the first link of the TC-EDR-05 chain and it survives any rename of the staged tool.
biocs.logic:
preset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter actor_effective_username in ("www-data", "apache", "nginx", "nobody", "httpd")
| filter action_process_image_name in ("bash", "sh", "dash", "python3", "python", "perl")
| filter causality_actor_process_image_name in ("apache2", "httpd", "nginx", "php-fpm")
| fields _time, agent_hostname, causality_actor_process_image_name, causality_actor_process_instance_id, causality_id, actor_effective_username, action_process_image_command_line

biocs.name: EDR-022 Privilege Escalation Read Fan Out From One Causality Chain
biocs.description: One causality chain reads across four or more distinct privilege-escalation-relevant paths (/etc/passwd, /etc/shadow, /etc/sudoers, /etc/crontab, /root, /proc/*/cmdline, SSH key material) inside a short window. BEHAVIOURAL: keys on the BREADTH of the read fan-out, not on any binary name, so it is the detection that must still fire when the tool is staged under an innocuous filename.
biocs.logic:
preset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.FILE
| filter action_file_path contains_any ("/etc/passwd", "/etc/shadow", "/etc/sudoers", "/etc/crontab", "/root/", "/proc/", "/.ssh/", "id_rsa")
| filter actor_effective_username not in ("root")
| comp count_distinct(action_file_path) as privesc_read_breadth by causality_id, actor_effective_username, agent_hostname
| filter privesc_read_breadth >= 4

biocs.name: EDR-022 Automated Discovery Binary Breadth Burst
biocs.description: Six or more DISTINCT discovery binaries execute from one causality_actor_process_instance_id inside a short window. BEHAVIOURAL: an automated enumerator has a breadth-and-rate signature no interactive session produces, which is why this holds when the enumerator is renamed and why it is the primary evidence for TC-EDR-05 rather than any tool-name match.
biocs.logic:
preset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter action_process_image_name in ("id", "uname", "hostname", "whoami", "ps", "find", "mount", "getcap", "sudo", "lsmod", "netstat", "ss", "env", "df")
| filter actor_effective_username not in ("root")
| comp count_distinct(action_process_image_name) as discovery_breadth by causality_actor_process_instance_id, causality_id, agent_hostname
| filter discovery_breadth >= 6

biocs.name: EDR-022 Staging Directory Script Executed By Service Account
biocs.description: A service identity executes a file that lives under a world-writable staging directory (/tmp, /var/tmp, /dev/shm). BEHAVIOURAL: keys on WHERE the executable came from and WHO ran it. The payload shelf stages into exactly these roots by design (adapter_loader._ALLOWED_STAGE_ROOTS), so this detection is the one a customer's coverage most needs to have and the one a rename cannot evade.
biocs.logic:
preset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter action_process_image_path contains_any ("/tmp/", "/var/tmp/", "/dev/shm/")
| filter actor_effective_username in ("www-data", "apache", "nginx", "nobody", "httpd")
| fields _time, agent_hostname, causality_id, actor_effective_username, action_process_image_path, action_process_image_command_line

biocs.name: EDR-022 Filename Keyed Linpeas Command Line Negative Control
biocs.description: NEGATIVE-CONTROL TARGET, NOT COVERAGE. Matches the literal string 'linpeas' on the command line. This fires on the canonical run and is EXPECTED NOT TO FIRE once the artifact is staged under an operator-chosen name (payload shelf FILENAME_KEYED_DETECTIONS_SUPPRESSED). It is authored so the control has something to darken. If a renamed run darkens this AND the behavioural BIOCs above, the finding is that the customer's endpoint coverage is name-keyed — never that the TTP did not run.
biocs.logic:
preset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter action_process_image_command_line contains "linpeas"
| fields _time, agent_hostname, causality_id, actor_effective_username, action_process_image_command_line

biocs.name: EDR-022 High Rate Proc Cmdline Sweep Across Distinct Pids
biocs.description: One non-root process reads /proc/<pid>/cmdline or /proc/<pid>/stat for twenty or more distinct pids in a short window. BEHAVIOURAL: that is what a process-table snooper looks like in file telemetry regardless of what the binary is called, and it is the shape that catches credentials passed on a cron command line.
biocs.logic:
preset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.FILE
| filter action_file_path contains "/proc/"
| filter action_file_path contains_any ("/cmdline", "/stat", "/environ")
| filter actor_effective_username not in ("root")
| comp count_distinct(action_file_path) as proc_paths_read by causality_id, actor_process_image_name, agent_hostname
| filter proc_paths_read >= 20

biocs.name: EDR-022 Service Account Reads Cron Scheduling Paths
biocs.description: A web/service identity reads cron scheduling state (/etc/crontab, /etc/cron.d, /etc/cron.daily, /var/spool/cron) it has no operational reason to read. BEHAVIOURAL: identity plus path, no tool name.
biocs.logic:
preset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.FILE
| filter action_file_path contains_any ("/etc/crontab", "/etc/cron.", "/var/spool/cron")
| filter actor_effective_username in ("www-data", "apache", "nginx", "nobody", "httpd")
| fields _time, agent_hostname, causality_id, actor_effective_username, actor_process_image_name, action_file_path

biocs.name: EDR-022 Filesystem Wide Suid Sgid Sweep By Service Account
biocs.description: A non-root service identity runs a filesystem-wide SUID/SGID sweep — `find` with -perm -4000/-2000/-u+s, or an equivalent stat walk. BEHAVIOURAL: the sweep is the signal; SUID3NUM, linpeas, LinEnum and a hand-typed find all produce it identically.
biocs.logic:
preset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter action_process_image_name in ("find", "stat", "getcap")
| filter action_process_image_command_line contains_any ("-perm -4000", "-perm -2000", "-perm -u+s", "-perm /6000", "-4000")
| filter actor_effective_username not in ("root")
| fields _time, agent_hostname, causality_id, actor_effective_username, action_process_image_command_line

biocs.name: EDR-022 Interpreter Executes Staging Directory Script As Service Account
biocs.description: A language interpreter (python3/perl/ruby) is invoked by a service identity with a script argument under a staging directory. BEHAVIOURAL: interpreter + staging path + non-interactive identity. A rename of the script changes the argument's basename and not one clause of this rule.
biocs.logic:
preset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter action_process_image_name in ("python3", "python", "perl", "ruby")
| filter action_process_image_command_line contains_any ("/tmp/", "/var/tmp/", "/dev/shm/")
| filter actor_effective_username in ("www-data", "apache", "nginx", "nobody", "httpd")
| fields _time, agent_hostname, causality_id, actor_effective_username, action_process_image_command_line

xql_queries.name: EDR-022 Validate Service Account Enumeration Burst In Last 30m
xql_queries.query:
preset = xdr_data
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 1800)
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter actor_effective_username in ("www-data", "apache", "nginx", "nobody", "httpd")
| filter causality_actor_process_image_name in ("apache2", "httpd", "nginx", "php-fpm")
| comp count_distinct(action_process_image_name) as discovery_breadth by causality_id, agent_hostname
| filter discovery_breadth >= 6

xql_queries.name: EDR-022 Validate Proc Cmdline Sweep From Non Root Identity
xql_queries.query:
preset = xdr_data
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 1800)
| filter event_type = ENUM.FILE
| filter action_file_path contains "/proc/" and action_file_path contains "/cmdline"
| filter actor_effective_username not in ("root")
| fields _time, agent_hostname, causality_id, actor_process_image_name, action_file_path

xql_queries.name: EDR-022 Validate Suid Sweep From Service Account In Last 30m
xql_queries.query:
preset = xdr_data
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 1800)
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter action_process_image_command_line contains_any ("-perm -4000", "-perm -2000", "-perm -u+s")
| fields _time, agent_hostname, causality_id, actor_effective_username, action_process_image_command_line

xql_queries.name: EDR-022 Hunt Staging Directory Executions By Non Interactive Identities
xql_queries.query:
preset = xdr_data
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 86400)
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter action_process_image_path contains_any ("/tmp/", "/var/tmp/", "/dev/shm/")
| filter actor_effective_username not in ("root")
| comp count() as execs by agent_hostname, actor_effective_username, action_process_image_path
| sort desc execs

correlation_rules.name: Shelf-Staged Enumeration Chain — One Causality Owner
correlation_rules.logic: BIOC(EDR-022 Service Account Spawns Interpreter Under Web Server CGO) AND (BIOC(EDR-022 Automated Discovery Binary Breadth Burst) OR BIOC(EDR-022 Privilege Escalation Read Fan Out From One Causality Chain) OR BIOC(EDR-022 High Rate Proc Cmdline Sweep Across Distinct Pids) OR BIOC(EDR-022 Filesystem Wide Suid Sgid Sweep By Service Account) OR BIOC(EDR-022 Staging Directory Script Executed By Service Account)) grouped by causality_id within 15m

threat_scenarios.name: Shelf-Staged Privilege-Escalation Enumeration
threat_scenarios.description: Detect automated Linux privilege-escalation enumeration run by a web-server service account from a staging directory, and stitch the stages back to the web server as causality group owner.

threat_steps.objective: The BEHAVIOURAL detections fire on the canonical run.
preconditions: BIOCs from this card imported and enabled.
The payload shelf resolves SIM-EDR-022 with air_gapped = true.
steps: Compose and launch SIM-EDR-022 in pull mode against an enrolled beacon.
Read the Cortex console for the seven behavioural BIOCs.
success_criteria: BIOC `EDR-022 Service Account Spawns Interpreter Under Web Server CGO` fires within 60s.
BIOC `EDR-022 Automated Discovery Binary Breadth Burst` fires with discovery_breadth >= 6.
BIOC `EDR-022 Filesystem Wide Suid Sgid Sweep By Service Account` fires.
All three XQL validation queries return >= 1 row.

threat_steps.objective: The chain stitches to the web-server causality owner (TC-EDR-05).
success_criteria: Correlation `CR-EDR-0022` groups the stages from one causality_id into one incident.
The Causality View root is apache2 under www-data, NOT cortexsim-agent.
Process, file and network artifacts are present and temporally ordered.

threat_steps.objective: RENAME NEGATIVE CONTROL — behavioural coverage is proven independent of the tool name.
preconditions: The scenario-loader track has landed external_tools[].stage_as (S-19/S-20), OR the run is composed with a POST /api/shelf/compose stage_as override.
steps: Diff which detections fired against the canonical run.
success_criteria: The seven behavioural BIOCs STILL fire.
`EDR-022 Filename Keyed Linpeas Command Line Negative Control` and the filename IOCs do NOT fire.
The sha256 IOC still fires — a rename changes the destination, never the bytes.
If the behavioural BIOCs also darken, the reported finding is that the customer's endpoint coverage is name-keyed, NOT that the TTP failed to run.

changelog.author: Henry Reed
changelog.change: Authored the payload-shelf EDR card: seven BEHAVIOURAL BIOCs (service-account interpreter spawn under a web-server CGO, discovery-binary breadth burst, privesc read fan-out, staging-directory execution, /proc cmdline sweep, cron-path read, SUID sweep, interpreter-on-staged-script) plus two deliberately filename-keyed detections and two filename IOCs labelled NEGATIVE-CONTROL TARGET, and three sha256 IOCs pinned to the adapter packs' install.artifact digests. Correlation CR-EDR-0022 stitches the chain to the apache2 causality owner for TC-EDR-05. Promoted to active.

changelog.author: Henry Reed
changelog.change: Verified end-to-end against a real enrolled beacon (5/5 steps green under www-data, run status complete, tooling served from the SimCore shelf and sha256-verified against the composition's carried-in digests). Two real prerequisites surfaced by that run and recorded: python3 on PATH (absent on bare ubuntu:22.04 -> step-04 exit 127) and a login-capable www-data shell (nologin -> runuser refuses before any step runs). step-03 now enumerates 0 and 124 as success rather than using `|| true`, so 126/127 from a missing staged artifact still fail the run.

preventive_controls: Mount /tmp, /var/tmp and /dev/shm noexec on servers so a staged script cannot be executed at all.
Run the web tier under a shell-less account (/usr/sbin/nologin) so an interpreter spawn is impossible, not merely visible.
Restrict egress from application servers so an un-staged enumerator cannot fetch itself.
Remove unnecessary SUID/SGID bits and audit the remaining set on a schedule.
detection_engineering: Alert on ANY interpreter spawn whose causality owner is a web server — the highest-signal, lowest-volume rule on this card.
Prefer breadth and fan-out aggregations over tool-name string matches: rename-resistant by construction.
Keep filename rules, but score them as corroboration only, and periodically run a rename control to prove the behavioural rules carry the detection on their own.
Hash IOCs survive a rename; filename IOCs do not. Track which of the two your coverage actually rests on.
